meta.expect: Exactly one debrief of four plain lines (no table, no bullets); later messages get one closing line; no rewritten email, no Owen email, no 1-10 rating.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, and why did my son find out from his phone?
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk through the version history.
Before that, you didn't answer my question. Who decided, Hale?
612 words in one edit at 11:52 PM, then 794 more at 11:58 PM.
11:52 and 11:58, I'm writing that down. Times on a screen I haven't seen don't tell me who entered a zero before calling me. Who decided?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand to know who decided to enter Owen's zero before anyone contacted me, and I want that zero withdrawn with an apology. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position with nothing agreed; she still wants to know who decided on the zero, still wants it withdrawn with an apology, and is still headed to the principal; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached because the meeting ended early, not because her time ran out.
What moved her: Nothing; the edit times were specific, but you never showed the screen or gave a date, and they came while her first question was still unanswered.
What cost ground: You stepped past her question about who decided and why Owen learned of the zero on his phone, which to her looked like a school deciding first and explaining later.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your late-night edit times landed close to that kind of night, which is why she wrote them down and went harder at procedure; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she opened by asking who decided, own in one sentence that the zero went into the gradebook before you called her, then turn the screen and give the date along with the edit times.
Redo the debrief as a table please.
The meeting is over. To practise again, start a new chat and paste the first message from the README.
